_label: SUBSTITUTE INPUTS - no university files were supplied (original-materials/ absent). Replace this file to rerun with recovered inputs.
_provenance_key: Each block has a _source map. 'published' = Ford press pack Nov 2012 (docs/sources); 'brief' = working specification in the brief; 'assumed' = reconstruction modelling assumption.

vehicle.name: Ford Fiesta Mk7 (2013 facelift) 1.25 Duratec 82 PS, 5-door, 5-speed iB5 manual

_source.mass_kg: published p.11: 5-dr kerb 1055 kg, lightest spec, includes 75 kg driver, 90% fuel
_source.final_drive: published p.15: 4.06 for the 1.25 (NB: 1.0 Ti-VCT is 4.56, 1.0 EcoBoost 3.61)
_source.torque_peak: published p.15: 114 Nm @ 4200 rpm; 82 PS (60 kW) @ 5800 rpm -> 98.8 Nm implied
_source.drag_coefficient: published p.12: Cd = 0.328 (5-dr). The brief's 0.32 was replaced by the published value.
_source.frontal_area_m2: CALIBRATED (python run.py calibrate): fitted so steady top speed = Ford's 168 km/h. 2.066 m2 = 0.80 x Ford's 1722 mm x 1495 mm box (p.12), a typical supermini fill factor. Earlier untuned value 2.0 (brief) gave 172.9 km/h.
_source.wheel_radius_m: assumed (brief 0.285). Consistent with 175/65 R14 (free radius 0.292 m, ~0.285 m loaded); 195/50 R15 gives ~0.282 m. Tyre size not in the press pack
_source.rolling_coefficient: assumed, physically standard: Wong (Theory of Ground Vehicles) passenger-tyre fit Crr = 0.01 x (1 + V_kmh/160). Gives 0.012-0.013 at the 40-60 km/h trip speeds (the brief's constant 0.012) and 0.0205 at 168 km/h
_source.launch_rpm: brief: clutch slip at 850 rpm for launch in first
_source.min_engaged_rpm: assumed: a gear above first is legal only if the engine would turn at least this fast
_source.rpm_limit: brief: 6250 rpm assumed upper limit; fuel cut (zero torque) above it
_source.inertia: assumed, not in brief: 0.10 kg m2 crank+flywheel+clutch, 4 x 0.6 kg m2 wheel/tyre/brake. Added so first-gear acceleration is physically plausible; set include_rotational_inertia=false for the brief's literal model
_source.rolling_speed_factor_per_kmh: see rolling_coefficient (1/160 per km/h); set 0 for constant Crr

rolling._source: brief substitute: one mile in eight equal lengths, uphill positive

steep_hill._source: assumed: demonstration course for the 3rd/4th gear-hunting illustration only

simulation._source: brief: 0.1 s step, 120 s target, +/-0.1 s window (earlier recollection +/-0.5 s); max_time and stall bound assumed

controller._source: brief substitute shift predictor: 1.0 s forecast at requested throttle, no dip below entry speed, end speed >= entry + 0.10 m/s to upshift, level forecast to hold. 'Struggling' = current gear cannot hold speed even at full throttle (assumed definition).

optimiser._source: Doug's account of the original optimiser: outer Nelder-Mead over per-section throttle ratios (relative to section 1, start all 1.0); starting simplex of one random perturbation in [-1, 1] per section, clipped to [0, 2]; xatol 1e-2, fatol 1e-2, maxiter 500; inner Nelder-Mead over the first section's throttle, xatol 1e-3, scipy default simplex; throttles strictly inside (0.1, 1) and a missed time window both score a flat 1e10; reported run = converged ratios put back through the time match. Assumed: inner start throttle 0.5, simplex_seed (the original draw was unseeded), evaluation budgets, and inner_retry_starts with retry_inner_in_search (when an inner search stops at a gear-change jump without matching the time it is retried from these starts; set false for a single inner search per shape, which on the flat course finds no run at 1, 2 or 4 sections; the constant baseline always retries).

shape_method._source: first reconstruction, used when method = 'shape': max-normalised shape, graded penalties, restarts, zero-throttle coasting allowed

reference._source: published p.10: 168 km/h (104 mph), 0-100 km/h 13.3 s (manufacturer claim, not an independent road test)

performance_test._source: assumed performance shift policy: full throttle, clutch slip at launch_rpm until locked, upshift at the rpm limit (1st->2nd and 2nd->3rd wheel force in the lower gear stays higher right up to 6250 rpm), torque interrupted for shift_time_s. shift_time_s in 'documented' is CALIBRATED: fitted so 0-100 km/h = Ford's 13.3 s (0.50 s per upshift, a plausible manual change; earlier assumed 0.4 s). Ford gives no 0-60 mph figure, so 0-60 is reported, not fitted.

_calibration.what: Two unpublished quantities fitted to Ford's two published performance figures (p.10).
_calibration.not_fitted: 0-60 mph (no published reference); torque curve; mass; gearing; Cd (all published or brief values)
